 Judgment

This appeal is by the petitioners against the judgment and award dated 18.10.2012 passed in M.V.C.No.2171/2008 by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Hassan ('the Tribunal' in short).
2.
The appellants are the petitioners and respondents are the respondents before the Tribunal.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts as pleaded by the petitioners is that, on 21.08.2008, the husband of petitioner No.1,
father of petitioners No.2 to 4 and son of petitioner No.5, one Rangaiah, the deceased, was killed at the spot while traveling in an auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-13/A-4374 near the house of one Somanna at Bittagodanahally on Hassan Road, as a result of hit by a Tipper Lorry bearing No.TN-27/M-0855.
The petitioners claiming to be the dependants have approached the Tribunal under Section 166 of the M.V.Act seeking grant of compensation of Rs.15 NC: 2023:KHC:20983 lakhs.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence of the parties by the impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.5,80,000/- with interest @ 6%
per annum.
The petitioners seeking enhancement of compensation have filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. I have heard the arguments of Sri.M.N.Ningaraja, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.D.Vijaykumar, learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was aged 40 years and earning Rs.8,000/- per month at the time of accident.
But the Tribunal has assessed it at Rs.4,000/-.
Future prospects was also not considered, amount under conventional heads is on the lower side and sought for enhancement.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the accident is of the year NC: 2023:KHC:20983 2008, the income is correctly assessed by the Tribunal.
The concept of future prospects was not in existence as on the date of the accident and therefore, the compensation assessed is just and adequate and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of both parties and also perused the materials on record.
8. The undisputed facts is that there was an accident on 21.08.2008 killing the deceased at the spot being the inmate of the auto rickshaw hit by a Tipper Lorry.

He was doing mason job and though it is alleged that he was earning Rs.8,000/- per month, having regard to the accident of the year 2008,
the income that could be assessed for a person with no proof of income is Rs.4,500/-.

If the Smt. Padma vs P. Narayana on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181750654/
3 principles of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1 is applied, future prospects has to be considered for the said income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:20983 the deceased was aged 40 years with no proof of income, future prospects that could be considered is at 25% and for the age of 40, the applicable multiplier as per Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2, will be '15'.

entities.text: Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Then the calculation of compensation would be as follows:
Rs.4,500/- + 25% future prospects = Rs.1,125/- = Rs.5,625/-.
Since there are five dependants, if 1/4th i.e., Rs.1,406/- is deducted, the net income comes to Rs.4,219/-.

Then the compensation towards loss of dependency comes to Rs.7,59,420/-
(Rs.4,219/-x15x12).

Under the conventional heads, towards loss of love and affection,
a sum of Rs.15,000/- each to the children and mother and towards loss of consortium at Rs.15,000/- to the wife is assessed, totally it comes to Rs.75,000/- and Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Then the total compensation comes to Rs.8,54,420/- instead of Rs.5,80,000/- assessed (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:20983 by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.2,74,420/-, it is just compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment is modified accordingly.

(iii) The appellants/petitioners would be entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,74,420/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization, excluding interest for the delayed period of 103 days in filing the appeal.

(iv) The respondent/Insurance Company is  directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of eight weeks NC: 2023:KHC:20983 from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(v) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
